question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool feature now, or require the broader federation identity and scope contract before adding core cross-gateway messaging?
rationale: Current source and docs keep gateways as separate trusted boundaries, while the requested feature would route messages and credentials across that boundary and has an open but unmergeable implementation attempt.

options.title: Design federation contract first
options.body: Require a maintainer-approved peer identity, scope, credential, and session-state contract before merging a core cross-gateway session primitive.

options.title: Repair the narrow peer PR
options.body: Allow PR #43656 or a replacement to proceed if it preserves the boundary model and proves fresh-install plus upgrade behavior across two real gateways.

options.title: Defer to plugin or MCP bridges
options.body: Keep core local-only for now and document supported external bridge patterns until a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design federation contract first
recommendation.body: Require a maintainer-approved peer identity, scope, credential, and session-state contract before merging a core cross-gateway session primitive.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history across session tools, gateway role policy, and multi-gateway documentation touched by this decision.
